text: 1. The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Thomas Cup is the men's world team badminton championship.

text: 2. The Uber Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Uber Cup is the women's world team badminton championship.

text: 3. The Sudirman Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Sudirman Cup is the world mixed-team badminton championship.

text: 4. The Davis Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Davis Cup is the major men's team tennis competition.

text: 5. The Billie Jean King Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Billie Jean King Cup is the major women's team tennis competition.

text: 6. The Ranji Trophy is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship.

text: 7. The Santosh Trophy is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Santosh Trophy is an Indian national football competition for state teams and institutions.

text: 8. The Durand Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Durand Cup is one of India's oldest football tournaments.

text: 9. The Duleep Trophy is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Duleep Trophy is a domestic first-class cricket tournament in India.

text: 10. The Irani Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Irani Cup is a first-class cricket match traditionally involving the Ranji Trophy champions and Rest of India.

text: 11. The Subroto Cup is primarily associated with which sport?
explanation: The Subroto Cup is a prominent international inter-school football tournament.

text: 12. The Vijay Hazare Trophy is associated with which format of sport?
explanation: The Vijay Hazare Trophy is India's domestic List A cricket competition.

text: 13. The Deodhar Trophy is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Deodhar Trophy is a domestic limited-overs cricket competition.

text: 14. The Ashes is contested between which two cricket teams?
explanation: The Ashes is the Test cricket rivalry between England and Australia.

text: 15. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is contested between which two cricket teams?
explanation: The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is the India–Australia Test series.

text: 16. The FIFA World Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The FIFA World Cup is the premier international football tournament.

text: 17. The Webb Ellis Cup is awarded in which sport?
explanation: The Webb Ellis Cup is the Rugby World Cup trophy.

text: 18. The Bledisloe Cup is contested in which sport?
explanation: The Bledisloe Cup is a rugby union competition between Australia and New Zealand.

text: 19. The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is associated with which sport?
explanation: The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup is an international men's field hockey tournament.

text: 20. The Hockey World Cup is organised under which international federation?
explanation: The International Hockey Federation is abbreviated as FIH.

text: 21. The ICC Cricket World Cup is organised by which body?
explanation: The International Cricket Council organises major international cricket tournaments.

text: 22. The FIFA World Cup is organised by which body?
explanation: FIFA is the international governing body associated with the football World Cup.

text: 23. The Thomas and Uber Cups are organised under which federation?
explanation: The Badminton World Federation, or BWF, governs international badminton.

text: 24. The Olympic Games are governed globally by which organisation?
explanation: The International Olympic Committee is the central Olympic organisation.

text: 25. The first Asian Games were held in 1951 in which city?
explanation: The inaugural Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.

text: 26. India's first individual Olympic gold medal was won by whom?
explanation: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold in the 10 m air rifle event at Beijing 2008.

text: 27. Who won India's first Olympic gold medal in athletics?
explanation: Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic athletics gold in men's javelin at Tokyo 2020.

text: 28. Milkha Singh became the first Indian to win an individual Commonwealth Games gold in which event?
explanation: Milkha Singh won the 400 m gold at the 1958 Commonwealth Games.

text: 29. P.T. Usha narrowly missed an Olympic medal in the 400 m hurdles at which Games?
explanation: P.T. Usha finished fourth in the 400 m hurdles at Los Angeles 1984.

text: 30. The Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports is located in which city?
explanation: The National Institute of Sports is located in Patiala, Punjab.

text: 31. The Khelo India Para Games were first held in which city?
explanation: The inaugural Khelo India Para Games were held in New Delhi.

text: 32. The Wankhede Stadium is located in which city?
explanation: Wankhede Stadium is in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

text: 33. The standard length of a cricket pitch is:
explanation: A cricket pitch is 22 yards, or 20.12 metres, long.

text: 34. A standard international field hockey match consists of:
explanation: Modern international hockey is played in four 15-minute quarters.

text: 35. A standard men's kabaddi match is generally played in:
explanation: A standard men's kabaddi match has two 20-minute halves.

text: 36. The standard height of a badminton net at the centre is:
explanation: The badminton net is 1.524 m at the centre and 1.55 m at the posts.

text: 37. In basketball under FIBA rules, a team has how long to move the ball from backcourt to frontcourt?
explanation: The backcourt-to-frontcourt time limit is 8 seconds under FIBA rules.

text: 38. The men's discus used in senior international athletics weighs:
explanation: The senior men's discus weighs 2 kg; the senior women's discus weighs 1 kg.

text: 39. In boxing, a technical knockout occurs when:

options.text: The contest is stopped by the referee, doctor or corner for safety
A boxer is disqualified for a foul
A boxer fails to beat the 10-count only

explanation: A TKO is a safety stoppage before a standard count-out or final-points decision.

text: 40. The 2026 Winter Olympics were scheduled to be hosted by:
explanation: Milano-Cortina in Italy was selected as host of the 2026 Winter Olympics; verify current-event developments separately.

text: 41. Which sport uses the term 'love' for a score of zero?
explanation: In tennis scoring, love means zero.

text: 42. The term 'deuce' in tennis generally indicates:
explanation: Deuce is reached at 40–40 in a standard tennis game.

text: 43. The Ryder Cup is associated with:
explanation: The Ryder Cup is a team golf competition between Europe and the United States.

text: 44. The Solheim Cup is associated with:
explanation: The Solheim Cup is the women's equivalent of a major Europe–United States team golf contest.

text: 45. The French Open is played on which surface?
explanation: The French Open, or Roland-Garros, is played on clay.

text: 46. Wimbledon is traditionally played on which surface?
explanation: Wimbledon is the major Grand Slam played on grass.

text: 47. The US Open tennis tournament is generally played on:
explanation: The US Open is played on a hard court.

text: 48. The Australian Open is generally played on:
explanation: The Australian Open is played on hard courts.

text: 49. The term 'Grand Slam' in tennis refers to:

options.text: Winning one match without losing a point

explanation: The four tennis Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian, French, Wimbledon, and US Open.

text: 50. The Hopman Cup is associated with:
explanation: The Hopman Cup is a mixed-team international tennis event.

text: 51. The Ryder Cup is played between teams representing:
explanation: The Ryder Cup is contested by Europe and the United States.

text: 52. The Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium is located in:
explanation: The Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium is a historic hockey venue in New Delhi.

text: 53. The Eden Gardens cricket stadium is located in:
explanation: Eden Gardens is located in Kolkata, West Bengal.

text: 54. The Narendra Modi Stadium is located in:
explanation: The Narendra Modi Stadium is in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

text: 55. The Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi is primarily known as a major venue for:
explanation: The Delhi stadium is a major athletics and football venue.

text: 56. The term 'hat-trick' most commonly means:
explanation: A hat-trick generally means three successes by one player or team in a match or contest, depending on the sport.

text: 57. In cricket, a hat-trick means:

options.text: Three wickets with three consecutive deliveries

explanation: A cricket hat-trick is three wickets with three consecutive legal deliveries.

text: 58. The Dronacharya Award is primarily given to:
explanation: The Dronacharya Award recognises outstanding coaches.

text: 59. The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award is associated with:
explanation: The Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honour for outstanding sporting performance.

text: 60. The Arjuna Award recognises:
explanation: The Arjuna Award recognises outstanding sporting achievement.

text: 61. The Dhyan Chand Award is associated mainly with:
explanation: The Dhyan Chand Award recognises lifetime achievement in sports.

text: 62. The first modern Olympic Games were held in:
explanation: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896.

text: 63. The Olympic rings traditionally represent:

options.text: The union of the Olympic movement and its continents

explanation: The rings symbolise the Olympic movement and its worldwide union; avoid memorising unsupported one-ring/one-continent mappings.

text: 64. The Commonwealth Games are associated with which organisation?
explanation: Commonwealth Sport governs the Commonwealth Games movement.

text: 65. The Asian Games are governed by which body?
explanation: The Olympic Council of Asia governs the Asian Games.

text: 66. The Paralympic Games are governed internationally by:
explanation: The International Paralympic Committee governs the Paralympic movement.

text: 67. The term 'LBW' belongs to which sport?
explanation: LBW means leg before wicket in cricket.

text: 68. The term 'offside' is most directly associated with which sports in common SSC questions?
explanation: Offside is a rule term used in several sports; identify the sport from the surrounding context.

text: 69. The term 'checkmate' belongs to:
explanation: Checkmate ends a chess game when the king is under unavoidable attack.

text: 70. The 'FIDE' is associated with:
explanation: FIDE is the international chess federation.

text: 71. The 'FIFA' abbreviation is associated with:
explanation: FIFA is the international football governing body.

text: 72. The 'BCCI' is associated with:
explanation: BCCI is the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

text: 73. The 'AIFF' is associated with:
explanation: AIFF is the All India Football Federation.

text: 74. The 'SAI' is associated with:
explanation: SAI is the Sports Authority of India.

text: 75. Which Indian woman became the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
explanation: Karnam Malleswari won bronze in weightlifting at Sydney 2000.

text: 76. Which Indian woman won an Olympic medal in boxing at London 2012?
explanation: Mary Kom won bronze in women's flyweight boxing at London 2012.

text: 77. Which Indian badminton player won an Olympic bronze at London 2012?
explanation: Saina Nehwal won bronze in women's singles at London 2012.

text: 78. Which Indian wrestler won an Olympic bronze at Beijing 2008?
explanation: Sushil Kumar won bronze in wrestling at Beijing 2008.

text: 79. Which sport uses a 400-metre standard outdoor track?
explanation: A standard outdoor athletics track is 400 metres per lap.

text: 80. In Olympic archery, the commonly tested bow category is:
explanation: Olympic archery traditionally uses the recurve bow category.

text: 81. The standard Olympic swimming pool length is:
explanation: The long-course Olympic pool is 50 metres long.

text: 82. A standard water-polo shot clock is commonly associated with:
explanation: Modern water polo uses a 30-second possession/shot-clock period; verify rule updates when necessary.

text: 83. A standard tennis tie-break is normally won by reaching at least:
explanation: A standard tie-break requires 7 points and a margin of 2.

text: 84. The 'touch-move' rule belongs to:
explanation: In chess, deliberately touching one's own piece generally obliges the player to move it if legal.

text: 85. The Olympic javelin is a field event in:
explanation: Javelin throw is a field event in athletics.

text: 86. The term 'relay' in athletics involves:

options.text: A team of runners carrying a baton

explanation: Relay races are team running events in which runners pass a baton.

text: 87. The 'Asian Para Games' are associated with:
explanation: The Asian Para Games are the major multi-sport para-sport event in Asia.

text: 88. Which item should be updated separately before SSC CGL 2026?

options.text: Latest tournament winners, hosts, records and rankings

explanation: Tournament winners, hosts, records and rankings are current-affairs facts and change by edition.

text: 89. Which is the safest way to study this Sports & Ranking module?

options.text: Sport/trophy or body—direct association—one stable clue

explanation: Stable associations should be learned first; volatile results should be updated separately.

text: 90. Which international body governs world athletics?
explanation: World Athletics is the international governing body for athletics.

text: 91. Which body governs international swimming?
explanation: World Aquatics governs international aquatic sports.

text: 92. Which body governs international table tennis?
explanation: The International Table Tennis Federation is abbreviated ITTF.

text: 93. Which body governs international basketball?
explanation: FIBA is the international basketball federation.

text: 1. ISRO was formally established in which year?
explanation: ISRO was established in 1969, succeeding the earlier INCOSPAR framework.

text: 2. Who is widely called the Father of the Indian Space Programme?
explanation: Vikram Sarabhai laid the institutional foundation of India's space programme.

text: 3. India's first artificial satellite was:
explanation: Aryabhata was India's first satellite, launched in 1975 with Soviet assistance.

text: 4. India's first person in space was:
explanation: Rakesh Sharma flew aboard Soyuz T-11 in 1984.

text: 5. The Satish Dhawan Space Centre is located at:
explanation: SDSC is ISRO's principal spaceport at Sriharikota.

text: 6. The Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre is located at:
explanation: VSSC in Thiruvananthapuram is a major launch-vehicle development centre.

text: 7. The U. R. Rao Satellite Centre is located in:
explanation: URSC in Bengaluru designs and develops Indian satellites.

text: 8. The Space Applications Centre is located in:
explanation: SAC in Ahmedabad develops payloads and applications for communication and remote-sensing missions.

text: 9. India's primary spaceport for orbital launches is:
explanation: SDSC at Sriharikota is India's main launch site.

text: 10. Which launch vehicle is known as ISRO's workhorse for many satellite launches?
explanation: PSLV has been widely used for polar, sun-synchronous, Earth-observation and interplanetary missions.

text: 11. Which ISRO launch vehicle is designed for heavier payloads and GTO missions?
explanation: GSLV uses a cryogenic upper stage and is designed for heavier geosynchronous missions.

text: 12. LVM3 was earlier known by which name?
explanation: LVM3 was formerly called GSLV Mk III.

text: 13. Which vehicle is designed for launching smaller payloads on demand?
explanation: SSLV is the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle.

text: 14. Mangalyaan, or Mars Orbiter Mission, was launched using:
explanation: MOM was launched by PSLV-C25 in 2013.

text: 15. Chandrayaan-3's lander was named:
explanation: Vikram was the lander module of Chandrayaan-3.

text: 16. Chandrayaan-3's rover was named:
explanation: Pragyan was the six-wheeled rover.

text: 17. National Space Day in India is observed on:
explanation: 23 August commemorates the Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing.

text: 18. Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated mission to study:
explanation: Aditya-L1 is a solar observatory mission.

text: 19. The L1 point in Aditya-L1 refers to:
explanation: Aditya-L1 operates in a halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point.

text: 20. Gaganyaan is India's programme for:
explanation: Gaganyaan aims to demonstrate human spaceflight capability to low Earth orbit and safe return.

text: 21. NavIC is the operational name of:
explanation: NavIC means Navigation with Indian Constellation and is India's regional navigation system.

text: 22. The original core NavIC constellation consisted of how many satellites?
explanation: The original NavIC constellation was designed around seven satellites.

text: 23. NISAR is a joint mission of ISRO and:
explanation: NISAR means NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar.

text: 24. Project NETRA is associated with:

options.text: Space situational awareness and debris tracking

explanation: Project NETRA supports tracking of space objects and protection of Indian space assets.

text: 25. The main purpose of space situational awareness is to:

options.text: Track satellites and debris to reduce collision risk

explanation: SSA monitors the space environment, satellites, debris, and collision risks.

text: 26. The first artificial Earth satellite was:
explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 in 1957.

text: 27. The first human to travel into space was:
explanation: Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space in 1961.

text: 28. The first human to step on the Moon was:
explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon during Apollo 11 in 1969.

text: 29. The first artificial satellite to orbit the Moon was associated with:
explanation: Luna 10 was the first artificial satellite to orbit the Moon.

text: 30. Which telescope mainly observes infrared wavelengths and operates near Sun–Earth L2?
explanation: JWST is an infrared observatory operating near the Sun–Earth L2 region.

text: 31. The Hubble Space Telescope is primarily a:
explanation: Hubble is a space-based astronomical observatory.

text: 32. Voyager 1 is famous for:
explanation: Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.

text: 33. A geostationary satellite has an orbital period approximately equal to:
explanation: A geostationary satellite matches Earth's rotation and appears fixed over one equatorial point.

text: 34. The approximate altitude of geostationary orbit is:
explanation: Geostationary orbit is approximately 35,786 km above the equator.

text: 35. Low Earth Orbit is generally associated with:

options.text: A few hundred to roughly 2,000 km altitude

explanation: LEO is the near-Earth orbital region used by many Earth-observation and crewed missions.

text: 36. A satellite placed at Sun–Earth L2 is useful for:

options.text: Deep-space observation with a stable thermal and viewing environment

explanation: L2 is useful for observatories such as JWST because of its observing geometry and thermal environment.

text: 37. Which mission studied Saturn and its moons?
explanation: Cassini–Huygens explored Saturn and its system.

text: 38. Which mission performed a close flyby of Pluto?
explanation: NASA's New Horizons conducted the famous Pluto flyby.

text: 39. Which mission is associated with Jupiter exploration?
explanation: Juno is a NASA mission studying Jupiter.

text: 40. Which Indian satellite series is strongly associated with remote sensing and Earth observation?
explanation: IRS means Indian Remote Sensing satellite series.

text: 41. Bhaskara satellites were primarily associated with:
explanation: Bhaskara missions supported Earth-observation and remote-sensing studies.

text: 42. The INSAT system is primarily associated with:
explanation: INSAT satellites support communication, broadcasting, weather and related services.

text: 43. GSAT satellites are mainly associated with:
explanation: GSAT is a communication satellite series.

text: 44. Cartosat satellites are associated with:
explanation: Cartosat missions support high-resolution Earth imaging and mapping.

text: 45. Resourcesat satellites are associated with:
explanation: Resourcesat missions support natural-resource and land-use monitoring.

text: 46. Oceansat missions primarily study:
explanation: Oceansat satellites provide oceanographic and marine data.

text: 47. RISAT satellites are associated with:
explanation: RISAT missions use radar imaging for Earth observation, including through clouds.

text: 48. AstroSat is India's first dedicated:
explanation: AstroSat observes astronomical sources in multiple wavelength bands.

text: 49. The Rohini series is associated with:

options.text: Early Indian satellites and sounding rockets

explanation: Rohini refers to important early Indian satellite and sounding-rocket programmes.

text: 50. The APPLE satellite was important in India's development of:
explanation: APPLE was an early experimental communication satellite.

text: 51. The Indian National Satellite system is abbreviated:
explanation: INSAT stands for Indian National Satellite System.

text: 52. The Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System is abbreviated:
explanation: IRNSS is the system later given the operational name NavIC.

text: 53. Which ISRO centre is especially linked with launch-vehicle development?
explanation: VSSC is a major centre for launch-vehicle development.

text: 54. Which ISRO centre is especially linked with satellite design and integration?
explanation: URSC is the major satellite design, development and integration centre.

text: 55. Which organisation operates India's space programme?
explanation: ISRO is the Indian Space Research Organisation.

text: 56. PRITHVI Vigyan is associated with which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

explanation: PRITHVI Vigyan is an Earth-system science initiative under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

text: 57. The main purpose of a weather satellite is to:
explanation: Weather satellites support atmospheric observation, forecasting and disaster warnings.

text: 58. A polar or sun-synchronous satellite is especially useful for:

options.text: Repeated Earth observation under similar lighting conditions
Remaining fixed above one equatorial point

explanation: Sun-synchronous orbits are useful for consistent Earth-imaging conditions.

text: 59. A geosynchronous orbit means that a satellite's:

options.text: Satellite must be on the Moon
Orbital period matches Earth's rotation period

explanation: Geosynchronous means the orbital period matches Earth's rotation; geostationary is a special equatorial circular case.

text: 60. The Sun–Earth Lagrange point L1 lies approximately:

options.text: 1.5 million km from Earth toward the Sun

explanation: Sun–Earth L1 is roughly 1.5 million km from Earth toward the Sun.

text: 61. Which mission is associated with Venus exploration planning by India?
explanation: Shukrayaan is the name associated with India's proposed Venus mission; check current status near the exam.

text: 62. Which mission is associated with lunar exploration?
explanation: Chandrayaan is India's lunar mission series.

text: 63. Which spacecraft carried the Huygens probe to Titan?
explanation: The Cassini spacecraft carried the Huygens probe, which landed on Saturn's moon Titan.

text: 64. The International Space Station is primarily:

options.text: A multinational crewed research laboratory in low Earth orbit

explanation: ISS is a multinational crewed laboratory in low Earth orbit.

text: 65. The International Space Station is associated with cooperation among:
explanation: ISS is an international partnership involving NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA and CSA, among others.

text: 66. Which agency is associated with the European space programme?
explanation: ESA is the European Space Agency.

text: 67. Which agency is associated with Japan's space programme?
explanation: JAXA is Japan's space agency.

text: 68. Which agency is associated with the United States civil space programme?
explanation: NASA is the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

text: 69. Which agency is associated with China's space programme?
explanation: CNSA is the China National Space Administration.

text: 70. A cryogenic engine uses propellants stored at:
explanation: Cryogenic propulsion uses fuels and oxidisers stored at extremely low temperatures, such as liquid hydrogen and oxygen.

text: 71. The principal advantage of a multi-stage rocket is:

options.text: Discarding empty stages to improve efficiency and payload capability

explanation: Staging drops empty mass during flight and improves launch efficiency.

text: 72. A satellite's payload means:

options.text: The instruments or equipment that perform its mission

explanation: The payload is the mission equipment, such as a camera, radar, transponder or scientific instrument.

text: 73. A satellite's bus generally means:

options.text: The support structure and subsystems that operate the payload

explanation: The satellite bus provides power, control, communication, thermal and structural support.

text: 74. Which Indian mission is associated with studying the Sun's corona and solar atmosphere?
explanation: Aditya-L1 is India's dedicated solar mission.

text: 75. Which spacecraft carried the Golden Record?
explanation: The Voyager probes carry the Golden Records containing sounds and images from Earth.

text: 76. The first living creature to orbit Earth was:
explanation: Laika flew aboard Sputnik 2; later Belka and Strelka returned safely from orbit.

text: 77. Which Soviet spacecraft carried Laika?
explanation: Laika travelled aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957.

text: 78. Point Nemo is popularly known as:
explanation: Point Nemo is the oceanic pole of inaccessibility and is associated with controlled spacecraft re-entry discussions.

text: 79. Which mission is associated with the first soft landing near the lunar south-polar region by India?
explanation: Chandrayaan-3 achieved India's successful soft landing in 2023.

text: 80. Which Indian launch vehicle is most directly associated with Chandrayaan-3?
explanation: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by LVM3-M4.

text: 81. Which topic should be updated separately before SSC CGL 2026?

options.text: Latest launches, mission status, discoveries and space appointments

explanation: Space current affairs change rapidly, so update recent launches, mission status, discoveries and appointments near the exam.

text: 82. What is the safest way to study Space & Satellite facts?

options.text: Memorise every altitude and date first

explanation: Stable mission–agency–purpose associations should be learned before detailed technical specifications.

text: 83. Which statement best distinguishes NavIC from GPS?

options.text: NavIC is a telescope and GPS is a rocket
NavIC is India's regional navigation system, while GPS is the US global system

explanation: NavIC is India's regional navigation system; GPS is the US Global Positioning System.

text: 1. One Nation One Ration Card primarily provides:

options.text: Portability of food-security entitlements across India

explanation: ONORC allows eligible beneficiaries to access subsidised food grains from Fair Price Shops across states, subject to the system's authentication and portability framework.

text: 2. The UDAN scheme primarily aims to improve:
explanation: UDAN, or Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik, promotes affordable flights to underserved and unserved airports.

text: 3. Mission Amrit Sarovar focuses on:

options.text: Development and rejuvenation of water bodies

explanation: Mission Amrit Sarovar is a water-conservation and water-body development initiative.

text: 4. The National Single Window System is mainly a:
explanation: NSWS helps investors identify and apply for approvals; it is not a separate ministry.

text: 5. The National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to make India a:

options.text: Global hub for production and export of green hydrogen

explanation: The mission promotes green-hydrogen production, use, and export; its official 2030 production target is a key current-affairs fact to verify.

text: 6. AMRUT primarily deals with:

options.text: Urban water supply, sewerage and basic infrastructure

explanation: AMRUT focuses on core urban infrastructure such as water supply and sewerage.

text: 7. The Production Linked Incentive scheme primarily seeks to:
explanation: PLI provides incentives linked to incremental production or sales in selected sectors.

text: 8. Jal Jeevan Mission is popularly associated with:

options.text: Har Ghar Jal and rural household tap connections

explanation: Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide functional household tap connections and safe drinking water in rural areas.

text: 9. PMAY-Urban primarily addresses:
explanation: PMAY-U supports housing for eligible urban households through defined verticals and assistance mechanisms.

text: 10. PM MITRA is associated with:

options.text: Mega integrated textile and apparel parks

explanation: PM MITRA stands for Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel parks.

text: 11. PM Fasal Bima Yojana provides:

options.text: Crop insurance against specified natural risks

explanation: PMFBY is the flagship crop-insurance scheme for farmers.

text: 12. PM-KISAN provides eligible farmer families with annual income support of:
explanation: PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments, subject to eligibility rules.

text: 13. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY primarily provides:

options.text: Health insurance/assurance cover for eligible families

explanation: AB PM-JAY provides cashless hospitalisation cover for eligible beneficiaries under its scheme framework.

text: 14. PM SVANidhi targets:
explanation: PM SVANidhi provides working-capital support to street vendors.

text: 15. Stand-Up India facilitates bank loans primarily for:
explanation: Stand-Up India promotes greenfield enterprise loans for SC/ST borrowers and women through bank branches.

text: 16. MGNREGA legally guarantees up to how many days of wage employment to a rural household in a financial year?
explanation: MGNREGA provides a legal guarantee of 100 days of wage employment to rural households meeting the statutory conditions.

text: 17. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao primarily addresses:

options.text: The girl child, child sex ratio and women’s empowerment

explanation: BBBP focuses on valuing, protecting and educating the girl child.

text: 18. The core objective of PM Ujjwala Yojana is to provide:

options.text: LPG connections to eligible poor households

explanation: PMUY promotes access to clean cooking fuel through LPG connections for eligible households.

text: 19. Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana focuses on:
explanation: PMJDY seeks to provide access to basic banking, savings, remittance, credit, insurance and pension services.

text: 20. PM Mudra Yojana provides:

options.text: Loans to micro and small non-corporate enterprises

explanation: PMMY supports micro-enterprises through the Shishu, Kishor and Tarun loan categories.

text: 21. Startup India primarily promotes:
explanation: Startup India supports the startup ecosystem through recognition, facilitation and related measures.

text: 22. Digital India primarily aims to transform India into a:

options.text: Digitally empowered society and knowledge economy

explanation: Digital India promotes digital infrastructure, services and literacy.

text: 23. Skill India is associated with:
explanation: Skill India aims to improve employability and vocational skills.

text: 24. Atal Pension Yojana is primarily a:

options.text: Pension scheme for eligible subscribers, especially in the unorganised sector

explanation: APY provides a defined pension framework based on contributions and eligibility.

text: 25. PM-SYM is a pension scheme for:
explanation: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan is a contributory pension scheme for eligible unorganised workers.

text: 26. PM-KUSUM is associated with:
explanation: PM-KUSUM promotes decentralised solar power, solar pumps and related farmer-energy support.

text: 27. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana primarily promotes:

text: 1. How many types of makeup (vaibhavam) are traditionally used for Kathakali dance artists?
explanation: There are exactly five types of makeup (vaibhavam) in Kathakali: Paccha (green), Kathi (knife), Thadi (beard), Kari (black), and Minukku (shining) [53]. Each color represents a character's moral alignment and spiritual quality [53]. For example, Paccha represents noble and divine figures, while Kari is for demonesses [53].

text: 2. Which Indian classical dance form traces its origin directly to the ancient temple dance 'Sadir Attam'?
explanation: Bharatanatyam, native to Tamil Nadu, evolved from 'Sadir Attam' (also known as Dasi Attam) [87, 98]. It was historically performed by Devadasis (temple dancers) and was subsequently renamed and revived in the early 20th century [87, 88].

text: 3. Which classical dance form traditionally concludes with a high-difficulty sequence called 'Tarangam' where the dancer balances on the rim of a brass plate?
explanation: Tarangam is the defining climax of a Kuchipudi recital [108]. The dancer performs rapid rhythmic footwork while balancing on the sharp edge of a brass plate, often while carrying a water-pot on their head [6, 108].

text: 4. Which 15th-century saint-reformer is credited with founding the classical Sattriya dance of Assam as a medium of Vaishnavite devotion?
explanation: Sattriya was introduced in the 15th century by Srimanta Shankardev, who used it as an accompaniment to his 'Ankia Naat' plays in the Satras (monasteries) of Assam [103, 104, 107].

text: 5. The famous four-part play 'Nalacharitam', which holds a supreme place in classical Malayalam literature, is traditionally associated with which dance style?
explanation: 'Nalacharitam' was composed by the 18th-century writer Unnayi Warrier [54]. It is a masterpiece in Malayalam literature specifically written to be staged as a Kathakali dance-drama [54].

text: 6. Which Indian classical dance form is historically performed to Hindustani classical music rather than Carnatic music?
explanation: Kathak is the only classical dance native to Northern India and is set to Hindustani classical music [58]. It incorporates Persian elements and court aesthetics, while other southern dances rely on Carnatic music [58, 69].

text: 7. What does the term 'Mati-Akhora' refer to in the context of Indian classical dance training?

options.text: The basic hand mudras of Bharatanatyam
A set of 64 ground exercises in Sattriya

explanation: 'Mati-Akhora' (ground exercise) consists of 64 basic movements that prepare a dancer's body for the postures and geometry of Sattriya dance [106].

text: 8. What are the two main parts in Manipuri classical dance that correspond respectively to the feminine (Lasya) and masculine (Tandava) elements?
explanation: In Manipuri, Jagoi represents the graceful, circular, and feminine (Lasya) aspect, often depicting Rasleela [76, 77]. Cholom represents the powerful, athletic, and masculine (Tandava) drumming aspect [76, 77].

text: 9. Which of the following traditional dance forms is NOT a part of Odia culture, despite being a classical form of India?
explanation: Dalkhai is a folk dance of Odisha, Gotipua is a temple precursor of Odissi, and Paika is an Odia martial dance [52]. Kathakali belongs strictly to Kerala [52].

text: 10. The earliest detailed description of Mohiniyattam as a solo female temple dance is found in which 18th-century treatise?
explanation: The solo dance Mohiniyattam finds its earliest written mention in 'Vyavaharamala', composed in 1709 AD by Mazhamangalam Narayanan Namboodiri [75].

text: 11. Who was the pioneering Bharatanatyam exponent, theosophist, and first nominated female member of Rajya Sabha who founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai?
explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale founded the Kalakshetra school in 1936 to preserve and clean Bharatanatyam's heritage [88, 89]. She was the first woman nominated to India's Rajya Sabha [89].

text: 12. The legendary classical dancer Mrinalini Vikram Sarabhai, honored on her 100th birthday with a Google Doodle, was a renowned exponent of which two dance styles?
explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai mastered both Bharatanatyam and Kathakali [94]. With her husband Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, she founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad in 1949 [94, 95].

text: 13. In which of the following Indian classical dance forms are the rhythmic syllables ('bols') of the Pakhawaj drum primarily used to conclude the performance?
explanation: In Odissi, the concluding part of the Mangalacharan (prayer of invocation/conclusion) utilizes the 'bols' of the Pakhawaj drum to synchronize the final dance movements [85, 86].

text: 14. The classical sequence of Bharatanatyam (Alarippu to Thillana) and its musical system were structured in the 19th century by which group of musicians?
explanation: The Tanjore Quartet—composed of four brothers: Ponnayya, Chinnayya, Shivanandam, and Vadivelu—systematized the modern repertoire and Carnatic musical background of Bharatanatyam [98, 99].

text: 15. Alarmel Valli, celebrated globally as a leading exponent of the Pandanallur style of Bharatanatyam, is also trained in which other classical dance form?
explanation: Alarmel Valli is an Indian classical dancer who excels in Bharatanatyam (Pandanallur school) but is also trained as an exponent of Odissi [55, 56].

text: 16. What does the term 'Kalasam' refer to in the context of Kathakali performance grammar?

options.text: A pure-dance sequence of foot movements and rhythm
The white beard makeup of divine characters
The opening call of the drums
A sacred pot balanced on the head

explanation: Kalasam is a pure, abstract technical dance sequence in Kathakali that acts as a rhythmic bridge between dramatic passages [53]. Ashtakalasam includes 8 types of Kalasam [53, 54].

text: 17. Which ancient Sanskrit text, composed by Acharya Nandikeshvara, serves as a primary source manual for studying the mudras and postures of Bharatanatyam?
explanation: 'Abhinaya Darpanam' by Acharya Nandikeshvara is considered the primary, most authoritative guide for study of gestures, expressions (abhinaya), and hand mudras in Bharatanatyam [97, 98].

text: 18. Which of the following classical dancers of India is NOT an exponent of the Odissi dance form?
explanation: Mayadhar Raut, Kumkum Mohanty, and Kiran Segal are celebrated Odissi exponents [124]. Geetanjali Lal is a renowned Kathak dancer of the Jaipur Gharana [124, 125].

text: 19. Which world-renowned Mohiniyattam dancer was the focus of Vinod Mankara's acclaimed documentary 'Mohiniyattathinte Amma'?
explanation: The documentary 'Mohiniyattathinte Amma' is based on the life of Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, who is universally regarded as the mother/pioneer of modern Mohiniyattam [72, 73].

text: 20. In which year did the Sangeet Natak Akademi officially recognize Sattriya as one of India's classical dances, making it the first addition in the 21st century?
explanation: Sattriya of Assam was formally recognized as the 8th classical dance form of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in November 2000 [103, 104, 106].

text: 21. The classical vocal style 'Thumri', traditionally used to express romantic and emotional themes, originated and flourished in the court of which Nawab?
explanation: Thumri music originated during the reign of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Awadh, and is intimately tied to the expressive choreography of Kathak [68, 69].

text: 22. Which ancient Sanskrit temple-theatre tradition of Kerala, performed by the Chakyar and Nambiar communities, was inscribed by UNESCO on its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2008?
explanation: Koodiyattam is Kerala's ancient Sanskrit theatre, performed inside temple auditoriums ('Koothambalams') by Chakyars and Nambiars, and recognized by UNESCO in 2008 [110, 111].

text: 23. Who among the following received her Kathak training from Pandit Birju Maharaj and has been honored with the Padma Shri for her contribution?
explanation: Shobhana Narayan, a premier Kathak exponent and retired IAS officer, received her rigorous classical training directly from Pandit Birju Maharaj [60].

text: 24. The spiritual and classical songs known as 'Borgeet' are a unique vocal composition composed by Srimanta Shankardev and Madhavdev for which classical dance form?
explanation: Borgeet sangeet consists of highly structured classical songs composed in Brajavali by Srimanta Shankardev and Madhavdev, used in Sattriya dance [105].

text: 25. Yamini Krishnamurthy, honored with major national awards, is celebrated as a leading master of which two classical dance styles?
explanation: Yamini Krishnamurthy holds the rare distinction of being a top-tier performer and pioneer in both Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam [58, 102, 103].

text: 26. Who was the legendary Carnatic classical singer and the first musician to receive India's highest civilian honor, the 'Bharat Ratna'?
explanation: M.S. Subbulakshmi, celebrated as the 'Queen of Songs' by Nehru and national leaders, became the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1998 [123].

text: 27. The famous 'Tippani' folk dance, which mimics roof-compaction manual labor using long wooden sticks, is native to which region?
explanation: Tippani originated from Chorwad in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat [117]. It was danced by women who struck long wooden poles (Tippanis) on the ground while singing [117].

text: 28. The 'Raut Nacha' is a traditional devotional stick-dance performed during Diwali by the Yadav (Gwala) community of which state?
explanation: Raut Nacha is a traditional dance of the Yadav herding community of Chhattisgarh, performed during Diwali to reenact Lord Krishna's victories [116].

text: 29. The spectacular folk-theatre tradition 'Yakshagana', characterized by vibrant makeup, elaborate costumes, and loud drumming, is native to which state?
explanation: Yakshagana is a highly stylized, traditional theatre form that originated in the 16th century in coastal Karnataka [114].

text: 30. The spectacular 'Gaur Maria' ritual dance, where men wear magnificent headgears made of bison horns and cowrie shells, is performed by the Maria tribe of which state?
explanation: Gaur Maria is a powerful, energetic tribal hunt-dance of the Bison Horn Maria (Gond) tribe in Bastar, Chhattisgarh [114].

text: 31. In which fast-paced, acrobatic folk dance of Chhattisgarh do Satnami community artists build magnificent human pyramids to honor Guru Ghasidas?
explanation: Panthi is a highly energetic, fast-paced acrobatic dance of the Satnami community [121]. Radheshyam Barle was awarded the Padma Shri in 2021 for his mastery of Panthi [121].

text: 32. Which famous indigenous dance of Mizoram involves clashing crossed bamboo poles on the ground while dancers step in and out of the shifting grids?
explanation: Cheraw (popularly known as the Bamboo Dance) is a historic dance of Mizoram [113]. It set a Guinness World Record for the largest number of bamboo dancers [113].

text: 33. How many major regional styles of the semi-classical martial dance 'Chhau' exist in eastern India?
explanation: There are exactly three major styles of Chhau dance: Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha) [118]. Mayurbhanj is unique as it uses no masks [118].

text: 34. Which ancient ritual festival, celebrated by the Meitei community to please the gods, is considered the oldest precursor to Manipuri classical dance?
explanation: 'Lai Haraoba' (meaning the merrymaking of the gods) is a Meitei festival in Manipur that forms the oldest root of Manipuri dance [77, 78].

text: 35. The traditional female temple performance styles Tevitichiyam, Nangai Natakam, and Dasiyattam are early developmental forms of which classical dance?
explanation: These early, solo ritual dances performed by women within temples are historically linked to the evolution of Mohiniyattam in Kerala [73].

text: 36. Which of the following classical dancers of India is NOT an exponent of the Kuchipudi dance form?
explanation: Raja/Radha Reddy, Shobha Naidu, and Vedantam Sarma are iconic Kuchipudi exponents [57, 58]. Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair is a doyen of Kathakali in Kerala [54, 55].

text: 37. Which traditional folk-play dance of Bihar, based on the mythological story of a brother and sister, is performed during Kartik Shukla Paksha?
explanation: Sama Chakeva is a beautiful clay-toy and performance festival in Mithila (Bihar), celebrating the pure bond between siblings [113].

text: 38. The 'Kamala' folk dance, which mimics the rowing of boats and netting of fish, is performed exclusively by the fishermen of which region?
explanation: Kamala is an energetic, agricultural-mimicry dance performed by fishermen communities in the Mithila region of Bihar [115].

text: 39. Sangeeta Mazumdar was honored with the prestigious Casa de la, Spain in 2019 for her outstanding contribution to which Indian classical dance form?
explanation: Sangeeta Mazumdar is a prominent young Kathak artist who won the international Spanish honor for her cross-cultural dance representations [60, 61].

text: 40. The traditional satirical solo dance-theatre 'Chakyar Koothu', where a single performer tells stories from the Epics using heavy narration, belongs to which state?
explanation: Chakyar Koothu is an ancient, solo temple performance in Kerala where a Chakyar artist recites Sanskrit stories with witty social satire [113].

text: 41. How many basic talas (talams) form the structural foundation of Indian classical Carnatic music?
explanation: There are exactly 7 basic talas in Carnatic music: Dhruva, Matya, Rupaka, Jhampa, Triputa, Ata, and Eka [130].

text: 42. Which legendary musicologist is credited with organizing and classifying the immense array of Hindustani classical ragas into ten standard parent scales ('Thaats')?
explanation: Pandit V.N. Bhatkhande revolutionized Hindustani classical music by codifying the raga notation system and organizing them into ten standardized parent scales (Thaats) [129, 130].

text: 43. In which Mizo folk dance do performers wear the handwoven 'Pundum' shawl and welcome visitors during high-status feasts?
explanation: Khuallam (meaning the dance of the guests) is performed by guests arriving at agricultural festivals in Mizoram, wearing traditional handwoven attire [118].

text: 44. The devotional folk-dance 'Chu-Faat' is performed by the Lepcha tribe of Sikkim during the Pang Lhabsol festival to worship what?

options.text: The sacred snow-capped peaks of Mount Kanchenjunga

explanation: Chu-Faat is performed with butter lamps and green bamboo branches by Lepchas to pay homage to the protective mountain peaks, especially Mount Kanchenjunga [118].

text: 45. Which of the following classical dancers is NOT associated with the Odissi dance form?
explanation: Sonal Mansingh, Kumkum Mohanty, and Pratima Bedi are highly celebrated Odissi exponents [81]. Anita Ratnam is a contemporary dancer trained in Bharatanatyam and Mohiniyattam [81, 82].

text: 46. Who among the following classical dancers of India is a renowned exponent of Sattriya and received the Padma Shri in 2008?
explanation: Jatin Goswami is a legendary pioneer and choreographer of Sattriya, honored with the Padma Shri in 2008 for his lifelong contributions [104, 105].

text: 47. The famous santoor player Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is originally a resident of which state/union territory?
explanation: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma, who revolutionized the Kashmiri folk instrument Santoor into a mainstream Indian classical instrument, hails from Jammu & Kashmir [135].

text: 48. Which of the following classical dance forms usually begins with the invocation dance 'Alarippu' and concludes with the energetic 'Thillana'?
explanation: Bharatanatyam recitals systematically unfold in six stages, starting with 'Alarippu' (invocation) and ending with 'Thillana' (fast-paced rhythmic finale) [99, 100].

text: 49. Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam, honored with the Padma Bhushan in 1998, founded which premier institution in Madras in 1963 to promote Kuchipudi?
explanation: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam established the Kuchipudi Kala Akademi in Madras in 1963 to systematically train and popularize Kuchipudi outside Andhra Pradesh [107, 108].

text: 50. For an Indian dance form to be granted 'Classical' status by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, it must rigidly adhere to the rules, mudras, and expressions of which ancient text?
explanation: Adherence to the grammar, mudras, and aesthetic principles laid down in Bharata Muni's ancient 'Natya Shastra' is the fundamental criterion for classical recognition [51].

text: 1. The 'Tusu' festival is primarily celebrated in the tribal belt of Jharkhand. According to recent SSC CGL 2025 shifts, it is especially concentrated around the area between Tamar, Raydih, and which other location?
explanation: Tusu is a harvest festival celebrated in the Panch Pargana area of the Chota Nagpur plateau, specifically between Bundu, Tamar, and Raydih in Jharkhand. It concludes on Makar Sankranti.

text: 2. Which Kodava harvest festival is celebrated with the chants of 'Poli, Poli, Deva' and a ceremonial paddy harvest, in which Lord Iguthappa is invoked? (Based on exact SSC CGL 2025 PYQ)
explanation: Puthari (or Huttari) is the traditional harvest festival of the Kodava community in Coorg (Karnataka). It is marked by the ceremonial cutting of the first paddy crop, seeking blessings from Lord Iguthappa.

text: 3. During the Solung festival, which traditional rice beer is shared to promote social bonding among the tribesmen of Arunachal Pradesh? (Based on exact SSC CGL 2025 PYQ)
explanation: Apong is an indigenous rice beer brewed by the Adi, Nyishi, and Mising tribes. It plays a central ritualistic and social role during the Solung agricultural festival in Arunachal Pradesh.

text: 4. Which of the following festivals is celebrated by the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh to drive away evil spirits, and involves the performance of the traditional 'Popir' dance?
explanation: The Mopin festival is the primary agricultural festival of the Galo tribe in Arunachal Pradesh. It is celebrated to drive away evil spirits and is intrinsically linked to the graceful Popir dance performed by women.

text: 5. The Pongtu Festival is a major agricultural celebration observed to seek blessings from the supreme deity 'Rangkathok' before the millet harvest. Which specific tribe celebrates this?
explanation: The Pongtu festival is the most significant agricultural and religious festival of the Tutsa tribe, located primarily in the Changlang district of Arunachal Pradesh.

text: 6. The famous 'Hornbill Festival' of Nagaland is named after the Indian Hornbill bird. According to Naga folklore, what does this specific bird symbolize?
explanation: The Hornbill is deeply respected in Naga traditions, and its feathers heavily decorate their tribal headgears. In their folklore, the bird symbolizes 'boldness and alertness'.

text: 7. The 'Kumbh Mela' is the largest religious gathering on Earth. According to Hindu mythology, the festival's origin is tied to the dropping of 'Amrit' (nectar of immortality) during which mythological event?
explanation: The Kumbh Mela commemorates the drops of Amrit (nectar of immortality) that fell from the Kumbha (pot) during the 'Samudra Manthan' (churning of the cosmic ocean) between gods and demons at four places: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik.

text: 8. 'Ali-Aye-Ligang' is a vibrant spring festival marking the onset of seed sowing. It is uniquely celebrated with the Gumrag dance by which indigenous tribe of Assam?
explanation: Ali-Aye-Ligang is the most colorful festival of the Mising tribe in Assam. 'Ali' means legumes, 'Aye' means seed, and 'Ligang' means to sow. It is celebrated in the month of Phagun.

text: 9. The 'Wangala' festival, also known globally as the 'Festival of Hundred Drums', is a major post-harvest thanksgiving ceremony dedicated to the Sun God (Misi Saljong). To which state does it belong?
explanation: Wangala is the most important festival of the Garo tribe in Meghalaya. It marks the end of the agricultural year and involves rhythmic dances accompanied by exactly one hundred traditional drums.

text: 10. The 'Behdienkhlam' festival is a vibrant celebration intended to chase away the demon of cholera and seek a good harvest. Which specific community celebrates this in Meghalaya?
explanation: Behdienkhlam is the most important festival of the Pnar (Jaintia) tribe of Meghalaya. It is celebrated in July after the sowing period, involving the beating of roofs with bamboo poles to chase away evil spirits and diseases.

text: 11. 'Garia Puja' is a major religious festival celebrated to invoke the deity of livestock, wealth, and peace. In which state is it predominantly celebrated during the Hindu month of Chaitra?
explanation: Garia Puja is an essential tribal festival of Tripura. Devotees worship Lord Garia, usually represented by a bamboo pole, to seek blessings for a good harvest and peace.

text: 12. The ancient and ecstatic 'Madai' festival involves night-long tribal singing, dancing, and a procession of local deities honoring Goddess Kesharpalin Devi. In which specific geographic region is it most famous?
explanation: The Madai festival is a major cultural event for the Gond and Muria tribes of the Bastar district in Chhattisgarh, acting as a massive social and religious gathering.

text:
13. Consider the following statements about the 'Bihu' festival of Assam:
1. Rongali Bihu marks the Assamese New Year in spring.
2. Kongali Bihu is a somber, restrictive festival related to crop protection.
3. Bhogali Bihu is the post-harvest feasting festival.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: All three statements are correct. Bihu is a set of three festivals: Rongali (Bohag) in mid-April (New Year/sowing), Kongali (Kati) in October (crop protection, lighting lamps), and Bhogali (Magh) in January (harvest feast).

text: 14. 'Gowri Habba' is an important regional festival celebrated primarily by married women to seek long life for their husbands. It is celebrated exactly one day before which major Pan-Indian festival?
explanation: Gowri Habba (worshipping Goddess Gowri) is celebrated predominantly in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. It takes place exactly one day prior to Ganesh Chaturthi (Bhadrapada month).

text: 15. The 'Ashtami Rohini' festival is characterized by special temple rituals, Uriyadi (pot-breaking), and cultural folk displays like Pulikali. It is the regional name for which festival in Kerala?
explanation: In Kerala, the birth of Lord Krishna (Janmashtami) is celebrated under the name Ashtami Rohini. It marks the eighth day (Ashtami) of the dark fortnight in the month of Bhadrapada, coinciding with the Rohini Nakshatra.

text: 16. Which of the following spring festivals in Goa serves as the Konkani equivalent of Holi, and is famous for the vibrant 'Goff' and 'Tarangamel' dance processions?
explanation: Shigmo (or Shigmotsav) is the most prominent spring festival of the Hindu community in Goa. It celebrates the harvest and involves elaborate street processions, colored powder, and traditional folk dances.

text: 17. The 'Kharchi Puja' is a massive festival involving the worship of the 'Chaturdasha Devata' (Fourteen Gods) over a period of seven days. It is the most celebrated religious event of which state?
explanation: Kharchi Puja is a famous Hindu festival of Tripura. During this seven-day festival, fourteen local dynastic gods (Chaturdasha Devata) are carried to the Saidra river, bathed, and worshipped.

text: 18. The 'Ambubachi Mela' is one of the largest religious congregations in Eastern India. What unique mythological or religious event does this festival commemorate?

options.text: The annual menstruation cycle of Goddess Kamakhya
The harvest of the first tea crop
The victory of Goddess Durga over Mahishasura

explanation: The Ambubachi Mela is held annually at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam during the monsoon season. It is a unique Tantric fertility festival celebrating the annual menstruation course of the presiding Goddess.

text:
19. Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): The 'Losar' festival marks the beginning of the New Year for the Tibetan Buddhist community.
Reason (R): Losar is celebrated exclusively in the state of Sikkim and nowhere else in India.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
A is true, but R is false

explanation: Assertion (A) is true as Losar is the Tibetan New Year. However, Reason (R) is false because Losar is widely celebrated in several high-altitude Indian states with Tibetan populations, including Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh (Monpa tribe), and Himachal Pradesh, not just Sikkim.

text: 20. The 'Hemis Festival', featuring spectacular Cham (masked) dances by monks, is heavily celebrated in Ladakh. Who is the central figure whose birth anniversary is commemorated by this festival?
explanation: The Hemis Tsechu festival is hosted at the Hemis Monastery in Ladakh. It celebrates the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), who is credited with bringing Vajrayana Buddhism to the Himalayan region.

text: 21. 'Chhath Puja' is an ancient and rigorously observed Vedic festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his sister 'Chhathi Maiya'. In which Hindu calendar month does the main Chhath festival occur?
explanation: While Chhath is observed twice a year, the primary and most famous 'Kartik Chhath' occurs on the sixth day of the Kartika month (typically October/November), exactly six days after Diwali.

text: 22. The 'Sarhul' festival is the most important spring festival of the tribal populations in Jharkhand (like Oraon, Munda, and Ho). Which specific sacred tree is worshipped during this festival to mark the advent of spring?
explanation: Sarhul literally means 'Worship of Trees'. The tribes worship the Sal tree, which provides them with timber, leaves, and resin, believing that the protector deity of the village resides in it.

text:
23. Match the Indian regional 'New Year' festival with its corresponding state/community:
1. Ugadi -> A. Maharashtra
2. Gudi Padwa -> B. Kerala (Malayali)
3. Vishu -> C. Tamil Nadu
4. Puthandu -> D. Andhra/Telangana/Karnataka
explanation: Correct match: Ugadi is the New Year for Deccan states (Telugu/Kannada). Gudi Padwa is the Maharashtrian New Year. Vishu is the astronomical New Year in Kerala. Puthandu is the Tamil New Year.

text: 24. 'Navroz' (or Nowruz) is a major spring festival celebrated on the vernal equinox. Which specific religious community in India officially celebrates Navroz as their New Year?
explanation: Navroz is the Iranian/Persian New Year, celebrated prominently in India by the Parsi (Zoroastrian) community to mark the beginning of spring (usually around March 21st).

text: 25. The 'Saga Dawa' festival is often referred to as the 'Triple Blessed Festival' for Buddhists. What three major events of Gautama Buddha's life does it simultaneously commemorate?
explanation: Saga Dawa is the most sacred Buddhist festival, highly celebrated in Sikkim. It marks the holy full moon day of the 4th Tibetan month when Buddha was born, achieved enlightenment, and attained Nirvana.

text: 26. 'Nuakhai' is one of the most ancient and prominent agricultural festivals in India, celebrated a day after Ganesh Chaturthi. Its primary purpose is to welcome the new rice of the season. To which state does it belong?
explanation: Nuakhai ('Nua' meaning new, 'Khai' meaning food) is the premier agricultural festival of Western Odisha, where the first harvested crop is offered to the mother goddess Samaleswari.

text: 27. The 'Bathukamma' festival is a vibrant, colorful floral festival celebrated primarily by women. Which goddess is specifically worshipped as the 'Life Giver' during this nine-day festival in Telangana?
explanation: Bathukamma means 'Mother Goddess come Alive'. It is celebrated in Telangana during Navratri. Women create beautiful concentric layers of seasonal flowers and worship Goddess Maha Gauri.

text: 28. 'Bonalu' is another major traditional Hindu festival centered in Telangana. While Bathukamma focuses on Maha Gauri, Bonalu involves offering meals in earthen pots to appease which fierce deity?
explanation: Bonalu is celebrated during the month of Ashada. Devotees offer 'Bonam' (a meal of rice, jaggery, and milk) to Goddess Mahakali in gratitude for fulfilling their vows and to ward off diseases.

text: 29. The 'Lai Haraoba' festival is the oldest traditional root form of culture in its region. It is celebrated by the Meitei community to please the Umang Lais (Sylvan deities). To which state does it belong?
explanation: Lai Haraoba (meaning 'Merrymaking of the Gods') is a foundational festival of the Meitei people in Manipur, celebrated to honor the ancient forest deities (Umang Lai) through ritualistic dances.

text:
30. Consider the following statements regarding the 'Yaoshang' festival:
1. It is considered Manipur's equivalent of the Holi festival.
2. It is celebrated for 5 continuous days starting on the full moon of Phalguna.
3. The traditional 'Thabal Chongba' dance is a major highlight of this festival.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
explanation: All statements are correct. Yaoshang is the premier festival of Manipur, blending Hindu Holi traditions (colors/water) with indigenous Meitei culture, particularly the Thabal Chongba (moonlight dance).

text: 31. 'Chapchar Kut' is a highly joyful spring festival characterized by the rhythmic Cheraw (bamboo) dance. What agricultural milestone does this festival mark for the Mizo people?

options.text: The shearing of the sheep before summer
The first monsoon rains hitting the dry soil
The completion of clearing and burning forests for Jhum cultivation
The successful harvest of the winter crops

explanation: Chapchar Kut is the biggest festival of Mizoram, celebrated in March. It marks the completion of the arduous task of cutting and clearing jungles for traditional slash-and-burn (Jhum) agriculture, before the sowing begins.

text: 32. The 'Kambala' festival is a traditional, adrenaline-filled sport involving a muddy racecourse. What specific animal is raced by the farmers during this event in coastal Karnataka?
explanation: Kambala is an annual buffalo race held in the slushy paddy fields of coastal Karnataka (Tulunadu region). It is traditionally sponsored by local Tuluva landlords to thank the gods for protecting their cattle.

text: 33. 'Jallikattu' is a traditional spectacle in which a bull is released into a crowd of people, and participants attempt to grab the large hump on the bull's back. During which major festival does Jallikattu take place in Tamil Nadu?
explanation: Jallikattu is a famous bull-taming sport played in Tamil Nadu as a part of the Pongal celebrations, specifically on the third day known as Mattu Pongal, which is dedicated to cattle.

text: 34. The 'Ojiyele' (or Oriah) festival is an agricultural festival where men perform a fierce war dance holding swords. According to recent SSC shifts, which tribe of Arunachal Pradesh celebrates this?
explanation: The Ojiyele festival is celebrated by the Wancho tribe of Arunachal Pradesh in spring. It features pig sacrifices and a prominent war dance by the tribal men.

text: 35. 'Makaravilakku' is an annual festival held on Makar Sankranti, which attracts millions of devotees to witness a holy light (flame) on the Ponnambalamedu hill. At which famous temple is this festival hosted?
explanation: Makaravilakku is celebrated at the sacred Sabarimala Shrine of Lord Ayyappa in Kerala. The sighting of the celestial light (Makarajyothi) on the distant hill marks the climax of the pilgrimage season.

text:
36. Read the statements about the Goncha Festival of Bastar (Based on exact SSC CGL 2025 PYQ):
1.) Tupki, a mock gun made of bamboo, uses Goncha fruit as bullets.
2.) The chariot procession was started by Chalukya rulers.
3.) Rath Yatra begins on Ashadh Shukla Dashmi and ends on Dutiya.
Which of the above statements are correct?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is a deliberate chronological trap set by TCS. The Rath Yatra actually begins on Ashadh Shukla Dwitiya (Dutiya) and concludes on Dashami (Bahuda Yatra), not the other way around. The Goncha festival is unique to Bastar, Chhattisgarh, where tribesmen use 'Tupki' (bamboo guns) to fire 'Goncha' berries as a mock salute to Lord Jagannath.

text:
37. Fill in the blank (Based on exact SSC CGL 2025 PYQ):
Ladakhi new year (Losar) is welcomed with symbolic dough models of ________, sun, and moon placed in households.
explanation: During the Losar (New Year) festival in Ladakh, symbolic dough models of the Ibex, along with the sun and moon, are created and placed on the kitchen shelves as auspicious symbols to bring prosperity and a good harvest.

text: 38. A week-long Jaunsari tribal fair held in Chakrata, which offers thanks for the harvest and honors Santura Devi (a manifestation of Goddess Durga), is officially known as: (Based on exact SSC CGL 2025 PYQ)
explanation: The Bissu Mela is an important cultural festival of the Jaunsari tribe in the Chakrata region of Uttarakhand. It marks the harvesting season and honors Santura Devi. A major highlight is the traditional archery and sword-dancing.

text: 39. Which of the following is recognized as Asia's largest cattle fair, celebrated annually on Kartik Purnima at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak rivers?
explanation: The Sonepur Mela (also known as Harihar Kshetra Mela) in Bihar is Asia's largest cattle fair. It takes place in November (Kartik Purnima) at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak rivers, where elephants, horses, and cattle are traded.

text: 40. The world-famous 'Pushkar Fair' is an annual multi-day livestock fair and cultural fete in Rajasthan. Which specific temple, the only one of its kind in India, serves as the spiritual epicenter of this fair?
explanation: The Pushkar Fair is heavily associated with the Brahma Temple in Pushkar, Rajasthan (one of the very few existing temples dedicated to Lord Brahma in the world). Devotees take a holy dip in the Pushkar Lake on Kartik Purnima.

text: 41. The 'Tarnetar Fair' is a vibrant celebration famous for its beautifully embroidered umbrellas (Chhatris) and traditional folk dances like Hudo. It is held around the Trinetreshwar Temple in which state?
explanation: The Tarnetar Fair is celebrated in the Surendranagar district of Gujarat. It is essentially a matrimonial fair for the local Bharwad and Rabari tribes, believed to commemorate the Swayamvar of Draupadi.

text: 42. Which prominent cultural fair in Gujarat celebrates the mythical marriage of Lord Krishna and Rukmini, acting as a unique cultural bridge between the western coast of India and the Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh?
explanation: The Madhavpur Mela is held in Porbandar, Gujarat. According to folklore, Lord Krishna married Rukmini here. Because Rukmini is traditionally believed by some to be from the Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, the fair uniquely integrates Northeast Indian culture with western India.

text: 43. The 'Surajkund International Crafts Mela' is the largest crafts fair in the world, heavily showcasing the richness of Indian handicrafts, handlooms, and cultural heritage. In which state is it hosted annually every February?
explanation: The Surajkund Crafts Mela is held every year in February in Faridabad, Haryana. It provides a massive platform for artisans from across India and partner nations to display their traditional crafts.

text: 44. The 'Medaram Jatara' is officially recognized as the second-largest fair in India after the Kumbh Mela. Which specific tribal community of Telangana predominantly celebrates this biennial festival?
explanation: The Sammakka Saralamma Jatara (Medaram Jatara) is a tribal festival honoring two mother-daughter goddesses. It is primarily celebrated by the Koya tribe in the Mulugu district of Telangana.

text: 45. Often referred to as the 'Kumbh Mela of the Tribals', the Baneshwar Fair is held at the sacred confluence of the Som, Mahi, and Jakham rivers. In which state is this fair organized?
explanation: The Baneshwar Fair is held in the Dungarpur district of Rajasthan. It is the largest tribal fair in the state, drawing massive crowds of the Bhil tribe who come to worship Lord Shiva at the confluence of the three rivers.

text: 46. The 'Minjar Fair' is a famous festival celebrating the blossoming of maize shoots (minjar). During this festival, people offer minjars and coconuts to the river Ravi. To which state does this belong?
explanation: The Minjar Fair is a major week-long international festival held in Chamba, Himachal Pradesh, during the monsoon season (July/August). It celebrates agricultural prosperity, specifically the maize crop.

text:
47. The 'Kumbh Mela' is held at four sacred locations based on astrological alignments. Match the Kumbh Mela city correctly with the river it is situated on:
1. Ujjain -> A. Ganga
2. Nashik -> B. Shipra
3. Haridwar -> C. Triveni Sangam
4. Prayagraj -> D. Godavari
explanation: Ujjain is on the banks of the Shipra river. Nashik is on the Godavari. Haridwar is on the Ganga. Prayagraj (Allahabad) is at the Triveni Sangam (confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati).

text: 48. 'Raja Parba' is a unique three-day agricultural festival that celebrates womanhood and fertility. During this period, all agricultural work is suspended because it is believed that Mother Earth undergoes her annual menstrual cycle. In which state is this celebrated?
explanation: Raja Parba (or Mithun Sankranti) is highly celebrated in Odisha. For three days, no digging, plowing, or tilling of the soil is done to allow Bhudevi (Mother Earth) to rest during her menstruation, ensuring future fertility of the land.

text: 49. The 'Dhanu Jatra' holds the Guinness World Record for being the largest open-air theatrical festival in the world. Which mythological story is entirely enacted across a city during this festival in Odisha?

options.text: The epic battle of Mahabharata at Kurukshetra
The churning of the cosmic ocean (Samudra Manthan)
The episode of Lord Krishna and his demon uncle Kamsa
The exile and return of Lord Rama

explanation: Dhanu Jatra is held in Bargarh, Odisha. The entire town transforms into Mathura, and the river Jeera becomes the Yamuna. The festival dramatically enacts the mythological story of Lord Krishna's visit to Mathura to kill the tyrannical King Kamsa.

text: 50. 'Nabakalebara' is a grand and highly secretive ancient ritual associated with the Jagannath Temple in Puri, Odisha. What exactly happens during this specific festival?

options.text: The king of Puri temporarily abdicates his throne to commoners.
The temple doors are shut for exactly one year.
The massive wooden chariots are burned and submerged.
The old wooden idols of the deities are buried and replaced with newly carved ones.

explanation: Nabakalebara (meaning 'New Body') is a ritual observed mostly every 12 to 19 years at the Puri Jagannath Temple. The old wooden idols of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra, and Sudarshana are replaced by newly carved ones from specific Neem trees.

text: 51. The 'Bali Jatra' (Voyage to Bali) is celebrated to commemorate the glorious maritime history of ancient Indian traders who sailed to Bali, Java, and Sumatra. Where is this massive open-air fair held?

options.text: On the banks of the Hooghly in Kolkata
On the shores of the Arabian Sea in Gujarat
On the banks of the Kaveri in Tamil Nadu
On the banks of the Mahanadi in Cuttack, Odisha

explanation: Bali Jatra begins on Kartik Purnima in Cuttack, Odisha, along the banks of the Mahanadi river. People float miniature toy boats made of colored paper and banana tree barks in the river to remember the ancient mariners (Sadhabas).

text: 52. The 'Thrissur Pooram' is considered the mother of all temple festivals in Kerala. It features a spectacular face-off between two rival temple groups parading caparisoned elephants. Which central temple hosts this event?
explanation: Thrissur Pooram is held at the Vadakkunnathan (Shiva) Temple in Thrissur, Kerala. The festival involves a friendly competition between the Paramekkavu and Thiruvambadi temples, featuring massive elephant processions and the famous percussion ensemble (Ilanjithara Melam).

text: 53. The spectacular 'Vallam Kali' (Snake Boat Race) is an internationally renowned cultural event in Kerala. In which backwater lake is the prestigious Nehru Trophy Boat Race traditionally held during the Onam harvest season?
explanation: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race, featuring the massive 100-foot-long snake boats (Chundan Vallams), is held on the Punnamada Lake near Alappuzha, Kerala, usually on the second Saturday of August during the Onam season.

text: 54. 'Onam' is the most significant harvest festival of Kerala. According to Hindu mythology, whose annual homecoming from the underworld (Patala) is celebrated during this ten-day festival?
explanation: Onam commemorates the legendary King Mahabali. It is believed that during Onam, the spirit of the just and benevolent Asura king Mahabali visits Kerala. He was historically pushed to the underworld by the Vamana avatar of Lord Vishnu.

text: 55. 'Pongal' is a four-day harvest festival celebrated predominantly in Tamil Nadu. Arrange the four days of Pongal in their correct chronological order:

options.text: Bhogi Pongal, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal, Kaanum Pongal
Mattu Pongal, Thai Pongal, Kaanum Pongal, Bhogi Pongal
Kaanum Pongal, Bhogi Pongal, Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal
Thai Pongal, Mattu Pongal, Bhogi Pongal, Kaanum Pongal

explanation: The correct sequence is: Day 1: Bhogi Pongal (discarding old things), Day 2: Thai Pongal (main harvest day, boiling rice), Day 3: Mattu Pongal (worshipping cattle/Jallikattu), Day 4: Kaanum Pongal (family visits and outings).

text: 56. The 'Thaipusam' festival involves devotees carrying physical burdens (Kavadi) and heavily piercing their skin, cheeks, and tongues with skewers to show devotion. To which deity is this festival dedicated in Tamil Nadu?
explanation: Thaipusam is a major festival celebrated by the Tamil Hindu community. It honors Lord Murugan (Kartikeya, the god of war) and commemorates the occasion when his mother Parvati gave him a 'Vel' (spear) to vanquish the evil demon Soorapadman.

text: 57. 'Karthigai Deepam' is a highly revered festival of lights in Southern India, often considered an extension of Diwali. A massive fire beacon is lit atop the Annamalai hills in Tiruvannamalai to honor which deity?
explanation: Karthigai Deepam is celebrated when the moon aligns with the Krithika constellation. The massive fire lit on the Annamalai hill in Tamil Nadu symbolizes the infinite and formless pillar of light (Jyotirlinga) that Lord Shiva manifested as.

text: 58. Which major 10-day purification festival is celebrated by the Angami Naga tribe in February to cleanse the body and soul of all past sins?
explanation: Sekrenyi (also known as Phousanyi) is the premier festival of the Angami tribe of Nagaland. It is a festival of purification where men take a sacred bath in a specific well to wash away their misfortunes.

text: 59. The 'Aoling' (or Aoleang) festival marks the arrival of spring and the beginning of the New Year. Which specific Naga tribe, historically known for headhunting and facial tattoos, celebrates this festival in the Mon district?
explanation: Aoling is the most important festival of the Konyak tribe in Nagaland, held in the first week of April. It celebrates the end of the sowing season and is marked by feasts, traditional dances, and the firing of muzzle-loading guns.

text: 60. The 'Moatsu' festival is celebrated over three days with joyous dancing around a large fire, primarily to celebrate the completion of the sowing season. To which tribe of Nagaland does it belong?
explanation: Moatsu Mong is the primary festival of the Ao tribe in Nagaland, celebrated in the first week of May. After the strenuous work of clearing the fields and sowing seeds, the tribe celebrates with a period of recreation and feasts.

text: 61. The 'Lui-Ngai-Ni' is a state holiday and a major seed-sowing festival. It is uniquely celebrated collectively by various Naga tribes inhabiting which specific state?
explanation: Lui-Ngai-Ni is a common seed-sowing festival celebrated by all the Naga tribes (Tangkhul, Zeliangrong, Mao, Maram, etc.) residing in Manipur. It is held annually on 14-15 February to mark the beginning of the spring season.

text: 62. The 'Shirui Lily Festival' is hosted to raise awareness about an endangered, highly unique terrestrial lily that grows exclusively in the Ukhrul district. Which state promotes this festival?
explanation: The Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae) is the state flower of Manipur. It only grows on the Shirui Hill ranges in the Ukhrul district. The festival is organized by the Manipur government to promote eco-tourism and protect the flower.

text: 63. The 'Gangaur' festival is one of the most colorful and important festivals of Rajasthan. Which deity is primarily worshipped by both married and unmarried women during this festival?
explanation: Gangaur is a combination of two words: 'Gan' (Lord Shiva) and 'Gaur' (Goddess Parvati/Gauri). Unmarried women worship Parvati for a good husband, while married women pray for the health and long life of their husbands.

text: 64. 'Teej' is a joyful festival heavily celebrated by women in Rajasthan, Haryana, and Punjab. What is the primary seasonal/mythological event it celebrates?

options.text: The arrival of winter and the harvest of wheat
The summer solstice and the defeat of the sun demon
The onset of the monsoon season and the reunion of Shiva and Parvati

explanation: Teej marks the advent of the monsoon season (Sawan). Women dress in green, apply henna, sing folk songs, and ride swings tied to trees. Mythologically, it celebrates the reunion of Goddess Parvati with Lord Shiva after 108 births.

text: 65. The 'Hola Mohalla' is a three-day grand festival where Sikh warriors (Nihangs) display their martial arts skills, horsemanship, and mock battles. At which historical site is this primarily held?
explanation: Hola Mohalla was established by the 10th Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, in 1701 at Anandpur Sahib. Unlike Holi, which involves splashing colors, Hola Mohalla was created for Sikhs to demonstrate their martial prowess (Gatka) and military readiness.

text: 66. 'Baisakhi' is a major spring harvest festival in Punjab. Beyond agriculture, it holds immense religious significance for Sikhs because it marks the formation of the Khalsa Panth. In which year was the Khalsa established?
explanation: On Baisakhi day in 1699, Guru Gobind Singh baptized the 'Panj Pyare' (Five Beloved Ones) and established the Khalsa Panth (the community of initiated Sikhs), fundamentally transforming the Sikh religion.
