explanation: Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry decoration.

text: 39. The Ashoka Chakra is awarded primarily for what?
explanation: Ashoka Chakra recognises exceptional gallantry in situations other than battle.

text: 40. Who received the first Jnanpith Award for Malayalam?
explanation: G. Sankara Kurup won the first Jnanpith Award for Malayalam.

text: 41. Which award is associated with India's national academy for music, dance, and drama?
explanation: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award honours achievement in performing arts.

text: 42. Which award is associated with the National Film Awards' lifetime honour in cinema?
explanation: Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest cinema honour.

text: 43. Which award is given for outstanding performance in sports by Indian sportspersons?
explanation: The Arjuna Award recognises outstanding sporting performance.

text: 44. Which award honours adventure and mountaineering achievement?
explanation: Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award recognises adventure achievements.

text: 45. The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar is related to what?
explanation: It recognises contributions to promoting and developing sports.

text: 46. Which award is presented for excellence in mathematics and is often called the Nobel Prize of Mathematics?
explanation: The Abel Prize is a major international mathematics award.

text: 47. Which Indian-origin mathematician won the Abel Prize in 2007?
explanation: S.R. Srinivasa Varadhan won the 2007 Abel Prize for work in probability theory.

text: 48. Which award is associated with international science popularisation and UNESCO?
explanation: The UNESCO Kalinga Prize honours science popularisation.

text: 49. Which Indian received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913?
explanation: Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

text: 50. Who won the 2006 Booker Prize for The Inheritance of Loss?
explanation: Kiran Desai won the Booker Prize in 2006 for The Inheritance of Loss.

text: 51. Who won the 2008 Booker Prize for The White Tiger?
explanation: Aravind Adiga won the Booker Prize in 2008 for The White Tiger.

text: 52. Who won the 2022 International Booker Prize for Tomb of Sand?
explanation: The author–translator pair was Geetanjali Shree and Daisy Rockwell.

text: 53. Who won the Booker Prize 2023 for Prophet Song?
explanation: Paul Lynch won the Booker Prize 2023 for Prophet Song.

text: 54. Who won the International Booker Prize 2024 for Kairos?
explanation: Jenny Erpenbeck and translator Michael Hofmann won the 2024 International Booker for Kairos.

text: 55. Which award did Riken Yamamoto receive in 2024?
explanation: Japanese architect Riken Yamamoto received the 2024 Pritzker Architecture Prize.

text: 56. Which Indian singer received the Bharat Ratna in 2001?
explanation: Lata Mangeshkar received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

text: 57. Which musician received the Bharat Ratna in 2008?
explanation: Bhimsen Joshi received the Bharat Ratna in 2008.

text: 58. Which civilian award was conferred on Chiranjeevi in 2024?
explanation: Chiranjeevi was among the 2024 Padma Vibhushan awardees.

text: 59. Which civilian award was conferred on M. Venkaiah Naidu in 2024?
explanation: M. Venkaiah Naidu received the Padma Vibhushan in 2024.

text: 60. Which award did Sheetal Devi receive for her sporting achievements in 2023?
explanation: Para-archer Sheetal Devi received the Arjuna Award in the 2023 sports awards.

text: 61. Which award category recognises India's highest national film honour?

options.text: National Film Award for Best Actor

explanation: Dadasaheb Phalke Award is the highest honour for lifetime contribution to Indian cinema.

text: 62. The National Sports Awards are presented by which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

explanation: National sports awards are administered through the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

text: 63. Which award recognises outstanding contribution to Indian cinema by a filmmaker or artist over a lifetime?
explanation: Dadasaheb Phalke Award is the principal lifetime cinema honour.

text: 64. Which award is associated with excellence in science and technology research in India?
explanation: The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize recognises major scientific research.

text: 65. Who won the Abel Prize in 2024?
explanation: French mathematician Michel Talagrand won the 2024 Abel Prize.

text: 66. Which award was won by The Elephant Whisperers?

options.text: Academy Award for Best Documentary Short Film

explanation: The Elephant Whisperers won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Short Film.

text: 67. Which award is associated with lifetime achievement in classical music in Madhya Pradesh?
explanation: Tansen Samman is associated with Hindustani classical music and Madhya Pradesh.

text: 68. Which prize is associated with mathematics, while the Fields Medal is awarded to younger mathematicians?
explanation: The Abel Prize is a major annual mathematics prize.

text: 69. Which award is specifically linked to Hindi literary works published within a specified recent period?
explanation: Vyas Samman is a K.K. Birla Foundation award for Hindi literature.

text: 70. Which award is associated with outstanding coaches rather than players?
explanation: Dronacharya Award is for coaches.

text: 71. Which current-affairs information should be updated separately before SSC CGL 2026?

options.text: Latest Padma awards, Nobel/Booker winners, sports awards and major international prizes

explanation: Award winners and civilian-award lists change every year, so the latest one-year current-affairs list must be added separately.

text: 1. The three new criminal laws came into force across India on which date?
explanation: BNS, BNSS, and BSA came into force on 1 July 2024.

text: 2. Which law replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860?
explanation: BNS replaced the IPC and deals primarily with substantive criminal offences and punishments.

text: 3. Which law replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?
explanation: BNSS replaced the CrPC and deals with criminal procedure, investigation, and trial.

text: 4. Which law replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872?
explanation: BSA replaced the Indian Evidence Act and includes provisions for electronic and digital evidence.

text: 5. How many sections are in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: BNS contains 358 sections, compared with 511 sections in the IPC.

text: 6. How many sections are in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: BNSS contains 531 sections.

text: 7. How many sections are in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
explanation: BSA contains 170 sections.

text: 8. Which new punishment was expressly introduced in BNS for certain minor offences?
explanation: Community service is included as a punishment under BNS for specified offences.

text: 9. Which law specifically codifies the offence of snatching?
explanation: BNS Section 304 deals with snatching as a distinct offence.

text: 10. BNS omits the colonial term sedition and instead criminalises acts endangering what?

options.text: Sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

explanation: BNS Section 152 addresses acts endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.

text: 11. Which BNS section deals with terrorist acts?
explanation: BNS Section 113 deals with terrorist acts.

text: 12. Under BNS, murder by a group of five or more persons acting together on specified identity grounds is addressed under which provision?
explanation: BNS Section 103(2) covers group murder in the specified circumstances commonly discussed as mob lynching.

text: 13. Petty organised crime under BNS is associated with which section?
explanation: BNS Section 112 deals with petty organised crime.

text: 14. Which of the following is associated with petty organised crime under BNS?
explanation: Petty organised crime includes specified acts such as theft, snatching, pickpocketing, and organised ticket or betting activities.

text: 15. Under BNSS, an electronic communication used to give information about a cognizable offence must generally be signed within how many days?
explanation: BNSS permits electronic communication, with the informant required to sign it within three days.

text: 16. What is the basic meaning of Zero FIR?

options.text: FIR can be lodged at any police station regardless of territorial jurisdiction
FIR against an unknown person only

explanation: A Zero FIR may be lodged at any police station and later transferred to the police station with jurisdiction.

text: 17. BNSS requires forensic investigation for offences punishable with imprisonment of how many years or more, subject to the statutory conditions?
explanation: BNSS provides for forensic expert visits and videography for offences punishable with seven years or more, subject to the applicable implementation provisions.

text: 18. Under BNSS, a court should pronounce judgment within how many days after arguments conclude?
explanation: BNSS sets a 30-day period for pronouncing judgment after arguments, with a possible extension under the statutory conditions.

text: 19. BNSS requires the police to inform the informant or victim about investigation progress within how many days?
explanation: BNSS requires communication of investigation progress to the informant or victim within 90 days.

text: 20. BNSS mandates audio-video recording especially for which police activity?
explanation: BNSS provides for audio-video recording of search and seizure, including preparation of the seizure list.

text: 21. BSA expressly includes which items within the idea of a document?

options.text: Electronic records, emails and digital messages

explanation: BSA recognises electronic and digital records, including emails, server logs, messages, and similar records, within the document framework.

text: 22. Under BSA, electronic or digital records can have the same legal effect as paper records when what condition is met?

options.text: They satisfy the statutory requirements of authenticity and admissibility
They are always treated as inadmissible
They can never be primary evidence

explanation: BSA gives electronic and digital records legal recognition subject to the statutory requirements governing their proof and admissibility.

text: 23. Which provision of BSA is associated with the legal status of electronic or digital records?
explanation: BSA Section 61 is associated with the legal effect and admissibility framework for electronic or digital records.

text: 24. Which BNS section deals with sexual intercourse by deceitful means, including specified false promises?
explanation: BNS Section 69 creates the offence of sexual intercourse by deceitful means under its statutory conditions.

text: 25. Under BNS, gang rape of a woman under 18 years may be punished with what?

options.text: Imprisonment for life for the remainder of natural life or death

explanation: BNS Section 70(2) provides life imprisonment for the remainder of natural life or death in the specified case.

text: 26. BNS Section 226 is associated with which offence?

options.text: Attempting suicide to compel or restrain a public servant from official duty

explanation: Section 226 addresses attempting suicide with the specified intent to compel or restrain a public servant.

text: 27. Which statement correctly distinguishes BNS, BNSS and BSA?

options.text: BNS—civil law; BNSS—tax law; BSA—company law
All three deal only with punishment

explanation: BNS is substantive criminal law, BNSS is criminal procedure, and BSA concerns evidence.

text: 28. Which punishment is associated with first-time petty theft under the statutory BNS conditions involving low-value property and return of property?
explanation: BNS provides community service as an alternative in specified first-time petty theft circumstances.

text: 29. The BNS provision for causing death by rash or negligent driving and escaping without reporting is associated with which section?
explanation: BNS Section 106(2) deals with the specified aggravated hit-and-run situation.

text: 30. Which law governs the procedure for arrest, investigation, bail, trial, and related criminal processes?
explanation: BNSS is the procedural criminal law replacing the CrPC.

text: 31. Which law primarily governs admissibility and proof of evidence?
explanation: BSA is the evidence law replacing the Indian Evidence Act.

text: 32. Which law primarily defines offences and prescribes punishments?
explanation: BNS is the substantive criminal code replacing the IPC.

text: 33. A preliminary enquiry under BNSS for certain offences punishable between three and seven years is to be completed within how many days?
explanation: BNSS provides a 14-day period for the specified preliminary enquiry.

text: 34. The maximum total police custody period under the statutory remand framework remains how many days, although it may be split within the permitted detention period?
explanation: The maximum police custody period remains 15 days, though BNSS changes the window in which it may be authorised in parts.

text: 35. Which BNS provision deals with the offence of causing death by negligence generally?
explanation: BNS Section 106 deals with causing death by negligence, including its statutory sub-categories.

text: 36. Which BNS section is associated with simple theft?
explanation: BNS Section 303 deals with theft; Section 304 separately addresses snatching.

text: 37. Which distinction is correct under BNS?

options.text: Snatching is only a civil wrong
Theft is regulated only by BNSS

explanation: BNS separately identifies snatching, while theft is dealt with under its own provision.

text: 38. Under BNSS, summary trial is made mandatory for specified petty offences punishable up to what maximum term?
explanation: BNSS expands summary-trial use for specified petty offences carrying imprisonment up to one year.

text: 39. Under BNSS, a mercy petition after Supreme Court rejection of appeal or review is generally to be submitted within what period?
explanation: The statutory mercy-petition procedure contains a 30-day period in the specified situation.

text: 40. Which BNSS feature supports trial when an accused deliberately remains beyond the court's reach?

options.text: Trial in absentia under statutory safeguards

explanation: BNSS introduces a statutory framework for trial in absentia subject to prescribed safeguards.

text: 41. Which BNSS feature supports reporting an offence without being limited initially by territorial jurisdiction?
explanation: Zero FIR permits initial registration at any police station before transfer to the appropriate jurisdiction.

text: 42. Which concept is associated with the right of an arrested person to meet an advocate during interrogation?

options.text: Access to legal counsel subject to statutory conditions

explanation: BNSS retains procedural safeguards relating to legal counsel and arrested persons.

text: 43. BSA recognises electronic records in which form?

options.text: Digital files, emails, messages and server records, subject to proof requirements

explanation: BSA modernises evidence law by recognising electronic and digital records subject to statutory proof requirements.

text: 44. Under BSA, what is the general significance of an electronic record's authenticity?

options.text: Integrity and authenticity affect admissibility and evidentiary value

explanation: The reliability, integrity, and statutory certification or proof requirements matter when electronic evidence is admitted.

text: 45. What is the purpose of judicial notice under evidence law?

options.text: The court may accept specified facts without requiring ordinary proof
It removes the right to cross-examine
The judge must accept every newspaper report
It applies only to civil contracts

explanation: Judicial notice allows courts to recognise specified facts without requiring the usual formal proof.

text: 46. Which statement about BNS and sedition is most accurate for exam recall?

options.text: Sedition was shifted to the Evidence Act
Sedition was retained word-for-word as IPC Section 124A
Sedition became only a civil wrong
The word sedition was omitted and a new sovereignty-unity-integrity offence was created

explanation: The BNS omits the label sedition and contains a new provision concerning acts endangering sovereignty, unity, and integrity.

text: 47. Which offence is newly or distinctly highlighted in BNS as snatching?

options.text: Taking property suddenly or forcibly from a person in the statutory circumstances

explanation: Snatching is separately defined and punished under BNS Section 304.

text: 48. Which group is associated with BNS Section 112?

options.text: Organised petty offenders involved in specified theft, snatching or similar acts

explanation: Section 112 covers petty organised crime involving specified activities by groups or gangs.

text: 49. Which group is associated with BNS Section 113?
explanation: Section 113 deals with terrorist acts.

text: 50. Which BNS provision is associated with organised crime?
explanation: BNS Section 111 addresses organised crime, while Section 112 addresses petty organised crime.

text: 51. Which BNS provision is associated with grievous hurt?
explanation: BNS Section 116 contains the definition of grievous hurt.

text: 52. Under BNS, what is the broad importance of community service?

options.text: It replaces imprisonment in every case
It is a new statutory punishment for specified offences
It is a civil remedy only

explanation: Community service is a statutory punishment for specified offences, not a universal replacement for imprisonment.

text: 53. Which of the following is a procedural change associated with BNSS?

options.text: Greater use of electronic communication and audio-video recording
Replacement of evidence rules by tax rules

explanation: BNSS modernises criminal procedure through electronic communication, digital records, and audio-video documentation.

text: 54. Which of the following is an evidence-law change associated with BSA?

options.text: Recognition of electronic and digital records

explanation: BSA updates evidence law for electronic and digital records while retaining proof and authenticity requirements.

text: 55. Which authority introduced the three new criminal laws through parliamentary legislation?
explanation: BNS, BNSS, and BSA were enacted by Parliament and brought into force by the Central Government notification.

text: 56. The former IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act were replaced respectively by which sequence?
explanation: The correct sequence is IPC—BNS, CrPC—BNSS, and Indian Evidence Act—BSA.

text: 57. Which statement about the new codes is correct?

options.text: They were enacted in 2023 and came into force in 2024
They were enacted in 1954 and came into force in 1960
They apply only to one state

explanation: The three laws are 2023 enactments that came into force on 1 July 2024, subject to notified provisions and updates.

text: 58. What is the exam-relevant meaning of a cognizable offence?

options.text: Police may arrest without a warrant under the law's conditions
Only a High Court can register it
It is always a civil dispute

explanation: Cognizable offences permit police action including arrest without warrant under the statutory conditions.

text: 59. What is the exam-relevant meaning of a bailable offence?

options.text: Only the President can grant bail
It is always a civil offence
Bail is a statutory right subject to the applicable law

explanation: In a bailable offence, bail is generally a right under the applicable procedural law.

text: 60. Which term refers to the first information recorded by police regarding a cognizable offence?
explanation: FIR means First Information Report; under BNSS, electronic communication and Zero FIR are important related features.

text: 61. Which code replaced the old CrPC section 482 framework on inherent powers of the High Court?
explanation: BNSS Section 528 retains the High Court's inherent powers framework, subject to the statute.

text: 62. Which BNSS provision is associated with electronic information and FIR registration?
explanation: BNSS Section 173 contains important provisions on information relating to cognizable offences and electronic communication.

text: 63. Which BNSS provision is associated with investigation completion and report to the Magistrate?
explanation: BNSS Section 193 concerns the police report on completion of investigation.

text: 64. Which BSA topic concerns facts that courts may recognise without ordinary proof?
explanation: Judicial notice is the evidence-law mechanism for recognising specified facts without ordinary proof.

text: 65. Which area should be updated separately before SSC CGL 2026?

options.text: Official amendments, commencement notifications, and new legal current affairs

explanation: Because the new codes are recent, verify the latest official text, amendments, commencement notifications, and exam-relevant changes near the exam.

text: 66. Which of the following is a safe one-line recall for the three codes?
explanation: This is the essential three-code distinction for SSC recall.

text: 67. What is the key caution when memorising exact section numbers from generated notes?

options.text: Only old IPC numbers can be tested
Verify them against the official Act because amendments and source errors are possible
All generated explanations are automatically official

explanation: Exact section numbers should be checked against the official statutory text, especially for recently enacted laws.

text: 68. Which procedural record may be prepared through audio-video electronic means under BNSS?
explanation: BNSS supports audio-video documentation of search and seizure procedures.

text: 69. Which category is directly modernised by the BSA?
explanation: BSA directly modernises the treatment of electronic and digital evidence.

text: 70. Which category is directly modernised by the BNSS?
explanation: BNSS modernises criminal procedure and investigation, including digital processes and statutory timelines.

text: 1. Which organisation publishes the Human Development Index?
explanation: HDI is published by the United Nations Development Programme in its Human Development Report.

text: 2. Which three broad dimensions form the Human Development Index?

options.text: Health, education and standard of living

explanation: HDI measures a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living.

text: 3. Which organisation publishes the Global Gender Gap Index?
explanation: The World Economic Forum publishes the Global Gender Gap Report and Index.

text: 4. Which four areas are measured by the Global Gender Gap Index?

options.text: Economic participation, education, health and political empowerment

explanation: The four sub-indices are Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment.

text: 5. Who publishes the Global Innovation Index?
explanation: The Global Innovation Index is published by the World Intellectual Property Organization, with knowledge partners.

text: 6. The World Press Freedom Index is published by which organisation?
explanation: Reporters Without Borders, also known as RSF, publishes the World Press Freedom Index.

text: 7. Who publishes the Global Hunger Index?
explanation: The Global Hunger Index is associated with Welthungerhilfe and Concern Worldwide.

text: 8. Which is NOT a component indicator of the Global Hunger Index?
explanation: GHI uses undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, and under-five mortality; maternal mortality is not one of its four components.

text: 9. Who publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index?
explanation: Transparency International publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index.

text: 10. In the Corruption Perceptions Index, a score of 100 indicates what?
explanation: CPI scores range from 0, highly corrupt, to 100, very clean.

text: 11. Which organisation produces the Global Peace Index?
explanation: The Institute for Economics and Peace produces the Global Peace Index.

text: 12. Which country has traditionally ranked at the top of the Global Peace Index?
explanation: Iceland has traditionally been the leading country in GPI; verify the latest edition for current-rank questions.

text: 13. The World Happiness Report primarily measures what?
explanation: The World Happiness Report ranks countries using subjective well-being data and related explanatory factors.

text: 14. The Henley Passport Index measures what?
explanation: The Henley Passport Index ranks passports by access to destinations without a prior visa.

text: 15. The Henley Passport Index relies mainly on data from which organisation?
explanation: Henley uses exclusive data from the International Air Transport Association for its visa-access methodology.

text: 16. Which index was discontinued by the World Bank in 2021?
explanation: The World Bank discontinued the Ease of Doing Business report in 2021 after data-integrity concerns.

text: 17. Who releases India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index?
explanation: NITI Aayog is the nodal agency for India's National MPI.

text: 18. Which three dimensions are used in India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index?

options.text: Health, education and standard of living

explanation: India's National MPI groups indicators under health, education, and standard of living.

text: 19. Who publishes the Climate Change Performance Index?

options.text: Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute and Climate Action Network

explanation: CCPI is published by Germanwatch, NewClimate Institute, and CAN International.

text: 20. Which organisation publishes the Logistics Performance Index?
explanation: The World Bank publishes the Logistics Performance Index.

text: 21. Who publishes the Global Competitiveness Report?
explanation: The Global Competitiveness Report was a World Economic Forum publication; note that the regular report was paused after 2019.

text: 22. Who publishes the Energy Transition Index?
explanation: The Energy Transition Index is published by the World Economic Forum with partners.

text: 23. Which organisation publishes the Global Cybersecurity Index?
explanation: ITU publishes the Global Cybersecurity Index.

text: 24. Which ministry conducts Swachh Survekshan?

options.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

explanation: Swachh Survekshan is conducted by MoHUA under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban).

text: 25. Which Indian city has repeatedly ranked among the cleanest in Swachh Survekshan?
explanation: Indore has repeatedly topped or ranked among the leading cities; verify the latest edition for current ranking questions.

text: 26. Who publishes the Export Preparedness Index for Indian states and Union Territories?

options.text: NITI Aayog with Institute for Competitiveness

explanation: NITI Aayog publishes the Export Preparedness Index in partnership with the Institute for Competitiveness.

text: 27. The Export Preparedness Index broadly measures which areas?

options.text: Only export value and forex reserves
Policy, business ecosystem, export ecosystem and performance

explanation: EPI evaluates policy, business ecosystem, export ecosystem, and export performance.

text: 28. Which body publishes the Global Terrorism Index?
explanation: The Institute for Economics and Peace publishes the Global Terrorism Index.

text: 29. Which organisation publishes the Rule of Law Index?
explanation: The World Justice Project publishes the Rule of Law Index.

text: 30. Which organisation publishes the Democracy Index?
explanation: The Economist Intelligence Unit publishes the Democracy Index.

text: 31. Which organisation publishes the International Property Rights Index?
explanation: The Property Rights Alliance is associated with the International Property Rights Index.

text: 32. Which organisation publishes the Environmental Performance Index?

options.text: Yale and Columbia universities with partners

explanation: The Environmental Performance Index is produced by Yale and Columbia researchers with partner institutions.

text: 33. The SDG India Index is published by which body?
explanation: NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index for states and Union Territories.

text: 34. The India Innovation Index is associated with which institution?

options.text: NITI Aayog and Institute for Competitiveness

explanation: The India Innovation Index is associated with NITI Aayog and the Institute for Competitiveness.

text: 35. The State Food Safety Index is released by which organisation?
explanation: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India releases the State Food Safety Index.

text: 36. The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is associated with UNDP and which institution?

options.text: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative

explanation: The global MPI is associated with UNDP and OPHI at the University of Oxford.

text: 37. The Global MPI measures poverty through which broad dimensions?
explanation: Global MPI uses deprivations across health, education, and living standards.

text: 38. Which body publishes the Global Financial Centres Index?
explanation: The Global Financial Centres Index is associated with the Z/Yen Group.

text: 39. Which body publishes the World Investment Report?
explanation: UNCTAD publishes the World Investment Report.

text: 40. Which organisation publishes the World Development Report?
explanation: The World Bank publishes the World Development Report.

text: 41. Which organisation publishes the World Economic Outlook?
explanation: The International Monetary Fund publishes the World Economic Outlook.

text: 42. Which organisation publishes the Global Economic Prospects report?
explanation: Global Economic Prospects is a World Bank publication.

text: 43. Which organisation publishes the Global Trade Outlook and Statistics?
explanation: The WTO publishes its trade outlook and statistics reports.

text: 44. Which organisation publishes the Human Capital Index?
explanation: The World Bank publishes the Human Capital Index.

text: 45. Which organisation publishes the World Energy Outlook?
explanation: The International Energy Agency publishes the World Energy Outlook.

text: 46. Which organisation publishes the Global Gender Gap Report?
explanation: The World Economic Forum publishes the Global Gender Gap Report.

text: 47. Which index ranks countries by perceived public-sector corruption?
explanation: The CPI measures perceived public-sector corruption.

text: 48. Which index measures countries' innovation inputs and outputs?
explanation: The Global Innovation Index evaluates innovation ecosystems and outputs.

text: 49. Which index measures trade-logistics efficiency such as customs and infrastructure?
explanation: LPI assesses logistics efficiency, including customs, infrastructure, and shipment organisation.

text: 50. Which index measures national commitment to cybersecurity across multiple pillars?
explanation: The ITU's GCI assesses national cybersecurity commitment across its pillars.

text: 51. Which index measures the quality and independence of the press environment?
explanation: The World Press Freedom Index assesses the press-freedom environment.

text: 52. Which ranking is based on the number of destinations accessible without a prior visa?
explanation: Henley Passport Index ranks passport access by visa-free or visa-on-arrival destinations.

text: 53. Which index is a composite measure of peace using safety, conflict and militarisation factors?
explanation: GPI combines measures relating to societal safety, ongoing conflict, and militarisation.

text: 54. Which index evaluates gender parity rather than absolute development levels?
explanation: The Global Gender Gap Index focuses on parity between women and men across four dimensions.

text: 55. Which Indian index assesses states' progress toward Sustainable Development Goals?
explanation: The SDG India Index tracks state and UT progress toward SDG targets.

text: 56. Which Indian index assesses states' innovation ecosystems?
explanation: The India Innovation Index assesses state and UT innovation performance and ecosystems.

text: 57. Which Indian survey ranks cities on cleanliness and sanitation?
explanation: Swachh Survekshan is India's major urban cleanliness survey.

text: 58. Which report is discontinued and should not be treated as a current annual ranking?

options.text: World Bank Ease of Doing Business Report

explanation: The World Bank discontinued Ease of Doing Business in 2021; current questions should not use it as a live annual index.

text: 59. Which index is jointly associated with Germanwatch and NewClimate Institute?
explanation: CCPI is published with Germanwatch and NewClimate Institute, along with CAN International.

text: 60. Which ranking is associated with press-freedom watchdog RSF?
explanation: RSF publishes the World Press Freedom Index.

text: 61. Which report uses life evaluations collected through the Gallup World Poll?
explanation: World Happiness Report rankings are based substantially on subjective life evaluations from Gallup data.

text: 62. Which annual report should be treated as current-affairs material rather than a permanent static fact?

options.text: Latest India ranks in HDI, GHI, CPI, GPI and other editions

explanation: Ranks, scores, top countries, and India's positions change by edition and must be updated close to the exam.

text: 63. Which is the safest way to memorise an index?

options.text: Publisher — indicator measured — one stable feature
Only the top country from one year

explanation: For SSC, retain the publisher, what the index measures, and one durable feature; separately update recent ranks.

text: 64. The Global Risks Report is associated with which organisation?
explanation: The World Economic Forum publishes the Global Risks Report.

text: 65. The Global Liveability Index is associated with which publisher?
explanation: The Economist Intelligence Unit is associated with the Global Liveability Index.

text: 66. The World Giving Index is associated with which organisation?
explanation: The Charities Aid Foundation publishes the World Giving Index.

text: 67. The Global Slavery Index is associated with which organisation?
explanation: Walk Free publishes the Global Slavery Index.

text: 68. The Global Peace Index, Global Terrorism Index and Ecological Threat Register are associated with which institute?
explanation: These major peace and security publications are associated with the Institute for Economics and Peace.

text: 69. What should you do with old rank questions from the uploaded dataset?

options.text: Use the old rank as a 2026 fact
Keep publisher/dimension facts and update the rank and score from the latest edition

explanation: Rank and score questions are time-sensitive; retain the stable framework and update the edition-specific data.

text: 70. Which index is most directly linked to the International Telecommunication Union?
explanation: ITU publishes the Global Cybersecurity Index.

text: 71. Which Indian ranking is directly linked to FSSAI?
explanation: FSSAI publishes the State Food Safety Index.
